messages.author: 63cc02caac0434cf
messages.subject: ZIP distribution error
parts:
Hello, 

I have tried to make the ZIP distribution using the instructions on the website.

dZIP <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = integer(), lambda = double(), 
                 zeroProb = double(), log = logical(0, default = 0)) {
    returnType(double())
    ## First handle non-zero data
    if (x != 0) {
      ## return the log probability if log = TRUE
      if (log) return(dpois(x, lambda, log = TRUE) + log(1 - zeroProb))
      ## or the probability if log = FALSE
      else return((1 - zeroProb) * dpois(x, lambda, log = FALSE))
    }
    ## From here down we know x is 0
    totalProbZero <- zeroProb + (1 - zeroProb) * dpois(0, lambda, log = FALSE)
    if (log) return(log(totalProbZero))
    return(totalProbZero)
  })

registerDistributions(list(
  dZIP = list(
    BUGSdist = "dZIP(lambda, zeroProb)",
    discrete = TRUE,
    range = c(0, Inf),
    types = c('value = integer()', 'lambda = double()', 'zeroProb = double()')
  )))

But it gives me an error, "Error in rargInfo[[1]][[2]] : subscript out of bounds". I tried looking in the user manual but I cannot figure out whats wrong.

Thanks!

messages.author: 9b1f1220a2b07d1e
messages.subject: Re: ZIP distribution error
parts:
Hi Dirk,

When I ran the above code, I reproduced the error you reported. However, when I included the construction of the rZIP random generator as in the example, the distribution registers properly. This suggests to me that there's something misaligned with the internal r-function placeholder that's used when registerDistributions is called without an available r function.

Not sure what the real problem or solution is, but hopefully this will provide a workaround for now and a starting place for others looking to debug!

Ben

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: ZIP distribution error
parts:
Thanks for this, Dirk.

In fact, fixing that bug was already queued up in our development branch (devel) for our next release.

Also, you no longer need to use registerDistributions for a routine case.  If you just use your distribution in a model, it will automatically detect and register it.  If there is no "r" function, it will create a placeholder.  Just be sure to provide initial values for any nodes following the new distribution so that they do not need simulated initial values, because that would require a working "r" function.

Please let us know further problems.

-Perry
